answer: The tundra detector writes to island, and grove makes public every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, and hence the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 30 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 120 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
